target_customer: Retailers and DTC or wholesale brands that need unified sales, stock and customer analytics
problem: Retail teams kept sales and stock data in spreadsheets and disconnected systems; 42 built a hosted analytics stack with retail metrics and handled the data integration.
business_model: B2B SaaS analytics subscription with managed integration

founders.name: Cathy Han
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2013-04-29) lists her formerly at P&G; NEXT 36 class of 2011 per NEXT Canada.

founders.name: Nick Porter
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page; Benbria per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Lucas Lemanowicz
founders.background_notes: Named as part-time co-founder by TechCrunch in 2013.

founders.name: Sarah Hum
founders.background_notes: Named as part-time co-founder by TechCrunch in 2013.

competitors.name: Euclid Analytics
competitors.what: Offline retail analytics from mobile location data
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as an offline analytics rival

competitors.name: Nomi
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a rival

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many retailer data formats and systems into one warehouse with retail metrics is steady engineering with messy data work.

defensibility.rationale: Managed data integrations with retailers and brands become embedded in buyer workflows, though dashboards themselves are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company continued independently for more than a decade.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2013 and NEXT Canada reported that retail teams struggled to access sales data stored in spreadsheets and systems not designed for them.

branding.name_origin: TechCrunch (2013-04-29) says the name is a nod to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, where 42 is the answer to life, the universe and everything.

identity.voice_and_tone: Light, with jokes such as asking a store manager at AllSaints

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of fan community or merch; the name is shared by many unrelated companies.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable pop culture number but a hard to search single number name used by many firms.

outcome_analysis: 42 launched at TechCrunch Disrupt NY in April 2013, joined YC in Winter 2014 and moved from consumer engagement toward analytics for retailers and brands. It has served 100 plus brands over 10 plus years per its own site, with customers such as AllSaints and Frasers Group, and is active, so it appears to be a durable niche SaaS business without a large reported raise.
notes: Seed round date and amount unknown: NEXT Canada names Y Combinator and CRCM Ventures; Dealroom adds 500 Global and Springboard Enterprises and Extruct dates it May 2014 with about $830K, both aggregator only and unverified. The product described in 2013 was personal customer engagement and later changed to retail analytics, but no dated source states the pivot so it is not recorded. YC lists only Nick Porter; Han is named by TechCrunch and NEXT Canada. YC lists founded 2014 while TechCrunch shows a 2013 debut. NEXT Canada article date appears as January 2020. A different company named 42 Technology (UK) and Lucky (acquired by SPINS in 2025) appear in aggregators and are unrelated. Audit fix: the May 2014 round of about 830K is recorded from Extruct (a single aggregator, which labels the 830K a grant tied to Sephora Accelerate and lists the seed as N/A, so stage and amount are unclear). 500 Global and Springboard Enterprises are recorded from Dealroom (single database, no date or amount). Sephora Accelerate is an accelerator program with no amount found. SparkLabs is not recorded as an investor: Wellfound lists SparkLabs Group only as a partner and no other source was found. These entries probably overlap the first seed entry and must not be summed.
